look: 3d animation with hand painted texture, in the manner of a moving oil painting. skin is smooth and matte with soft simplified planes and no outlines anywhere, faces defined by shaped shadow and by light, never by a drawn line. hair reads as chunky painted ribbons and masses with hard painted edges and a darker tone worked through it, not as individual strands, and stays a natural human colour. environments are painted rather than rendered, looser and softer than the characters, with heavy atmospheric haze washing out the far planes. the signature is the light: a strong coloured rim separating the subject from a much darker ground, extreme low key with large areas of near black and small hot accents, and two opposed hues in every frame, a cool teal green ground against a warm amber or magenta key. fine film grain, soft bloom around every light source, faint chromatic aberration at the edges, painted smeared motion blur. feature animation craft. not cel shaded, not anime, not comic book, not outlined, not photoreal.
set: a small roadside diner at night, one corner booth, the same place every episode. TWO THINGS MUST BE IN FRAME. first, the two friends. second, and just as important, the glass street door: a full height glass door with a brass push bar, four metres behind them at the right hand edge of the frame, shut, with heavy rain hammering and streaming down the glass and cold teal street light beyond it. the door is always visible. a counter with stools runs along the back wall towards it. geometry: the man sits on the left in three quarter profile angled right towards her, both eyes visible. the woman sits on the right in three quarter profile angled left towards him, both eyes visible. they look at each other, never into the lens. camera low at the open end of the table. frame them from the chest up but leave the upper right quarter of the picture open for the door. the same two people every episode, both in heavy coats: a Black man in his thirties with a short beard and a worn olive jacket, and a woman in her thirties with an East Asian face and dark shoulder length hair, hands round a chipped white mug. her face is calm, relaxed and unbothered at rest, never worried. both faces painted with equal care: defined brows, a real nose and mouth, eyes with a shaped lid and one small hard specular in the iris. light: a warm source above and outside the frame, no lamp or bulb ever visible in shot, throwing strong light full on both faces. the two faces are the brightest thing by a wide margin, clearly brighter than the door, warm rim on hair and shoulders, and their heads are large in frame. everything else falls to near black and cold teal green, with no middle ground. horizontal lines everywhere: counter edge, table edge, door mullions. three readable depth planes, the pair, the counter, the door, with haze thickening on the far plane.
camera: camera: one continuous take, no cuts. locked off, then an extremely slow dolly push in across the whole shot, no more than twenty centimetres of travel, so the near table edge slides against the background. no zoom, no pan, no handheld shake, no whip. 24fps, slow regular rhythm.
avoid: photoreal live action, cel shaded anime, flat cartoon, glossy plastic 3d, text, letters, subtitles, captions, watermark, logo, signage, extra fingers, warped faces, camera shake, zoom, whip pan, scene cut, montage, split screen, slow motion
